title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Delamination Detection on 2920 Series
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 5nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Klaus Weber

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the 2920 Series system to detect and classify Delamination defects during final inspection inspection at the 5nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Delamination defects that are critical to yield at the 5nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the 2920 Series platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: 2920 Series
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Delamination
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 5nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all 2920 Series systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for final inspection monitoring in the 5nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: 2920 Series
Software Version: v11.3.894
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_5nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (154 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the 2920 Series system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Delamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 5nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 71 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.7% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-12-11
Wafers Tested: 33
Total Defects Found: 339
Defect Density: 107.91 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.8%
Capture Rate: 87.1%
Test Duration: 60 minutes
System Uptime: 97.4%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The 2920 Series demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Delamination at the 5nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
